questions.question: A genre is a category of texts that share what?
A story includes invented characters and events. Which broad category is it?
A narrative presents factual events from a person’s life, written by someone else. What genre is this?
A person writes an account of their own life. What genre is this?
A story includes magic in a world unlike the real one. Which genre is likely?
A narrative uses scientific possibilities and imagined future technology. Which genre may fit?
A fictional story is set during a documented historical period. What genre is this?
A brief story teaches a lesson through animal characters who speak. Which form is likely?
A story centers on clues and the solution to a crime. What genre is most likely?
A short personal account focuses on a meaningful experience rather than a whole life. What is it?
A play uses humor and mistaken identities to entertain. Which genre is most likely?
A play traces a serious downfall caused partly by a protagonist’s choices. Which genre may fit?
A long narrative poem tells of a hero’s major journey. What form is this?
A text uses exaggeration and humor to criticize a social practice. What genre or mode is this?
A story describes ordinary people and events that could occur in the present world. Which genre fits?
A text presents characters’ speech and actions through scenes meant for performance. What genre is it?
A student labels a text “fantasy” because one character has an unusual name. What evidence would better support the label?
choices: impossible or magical elements shape the story

questions.question: A novel set in the past includes invented characters alongside real historical events. What distinction matters?
choices: it must be a primary source
it is historical fiction, not a factual account in every detail

questions.question: A first-person account describes a person’s own memories and reflections. Which label is most precise?
choices: memoir or autobiography, depending on scope

questions.question: A text shares traits of mystery and science fiction. What is a sound conclusion?
choices: every text belongs to exactly one genre
genre is based only on length
genre depends only on the author
genres can overlap when a work uses conventions of more than one
